   - GDPR / HIPAA applicability for PHI and DSR workflow
   - Retention windows: access/audit logs vs application data vs backups/snapshots
   - Deletion SLA and how deletions map to backups / immutable snapshots
   - KMS/customer-managed keys capability for encryption at rest

2) Questions we promised to answer / confirm (we'll attach the short artifacts):
   - SOC 2 Type II: whether we have a recent Type II and the scope (we'll attach the summary)
   - Default retention values and how they can be adjusted by contract
   - Backup snapshot retention vs logical delete behavior and the deletion SLA timeline
   - Support for CMEK / HSM in Private deployment options

3) Next steps / asks: 
   - Kim (cc) will provide a short written summary + retention matrix (attached).
   - We will open the vendor security questionnaire in your portal and start filling answers; if there are high-risk controls you want prioritized, flag them.
   - Propose a 30-minute technical follow-up with Kim + Marcus next week to walk the retention matrix and evidence (suggested times: Tue/Wed 10–11am PT).

Attachments you will see in the follow-up email: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf, redwood_retention_matrix_acme.xlsx, redwood_backup_policy_snippet.txt

If that matches your expectations, we’ll start the questionnaire and lock a follow-up.

Thanks Ben — that recap is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side before we schedule the tech call:

- Can you confirm what you treat as a "backup" versus a "snapshot" in your platform? For our compliance team snapshots are often considered immutable copies and have different retention rules.
- Do you offer an explicit deletion timeline for data subject requests (we need to map a 30-day DSR window to your deletion pipeline)?
- For HIPAA: does Redwood support a customer-managed key option in hosted/dedicated so our KMS policies can apply?
- Regarding backups: do you provide WORM / immutable backup options or write-once retention tiers?

Also, please send the SOC 2 summary and retention matrix; I'll route to our infosec and privacy folks. If you could flag anything that you anticipate needing legal approval (e.g., unusually long backup retention required for operational reasons), call that out.

Sam Willis
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Health
sam.willis@acmehealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Willis <sam.willis@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle SLA alignment & evidence request

Hi Sam — appreciate the detailed questions. Short answers up front, followed by more details and attachments.

High-level:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II covering our platform and hosting controls for the period 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31. We can provide the auditor's report under NDA / signing portal; the attached PDF is a customer-friendly summary of scope and key controls.
- Backups vs snapshots: in our hosting model we maintain application-level backups (rotated daily, retained per the backup retention policy) and point-in-time snapshots for quick restore. Snapshots are stored in an immutable chain for the duration of the configured retention window; by default snapshots are retained 90 days.
- Deletion / DSR: standard deletion requests are processed within 72 hours from request and removed from active storage. Logical deletion is immediate; purging from backups follows the backup retention lifecycle (i.e., data may remain in backup snapshots until their retention expires unless a discrete legal hold or targeted purge is requested). For contractual DSR guarantees we can commit to a deletion SLA that includes a maximum time-to-purge from active systems and an agreed process for backup erasure where feasible (typical negotiated windows are 30–90 days depending on backup medium).
- KMS / CMEK: hosted Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP CMEK for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted API we offer a KMS integration option for enterprise customers (requires contract addendum). HSM integrations are available for Private deploys.
- WORM / immutable: we offer immutable snapshot tiers for customers on Dedicated and Private; Hosted customers can opt into immutable backups via our premium retention add-on.

Detailed notes (for your infosec team):
- Default retention matrix (attached):
   * Access / audit logs: 365 days (configurable 90–1095 days)
   * Application request logs (non-PII): 180 days default (configurable)
   * User-generated content / model inputs: logical delete at request (default sandbox) — purge from active storage within 72 hours; backup retention default 90 days
   * Backups / snapshots: default 90 days immutable chain; long-term archival up to 2 years available on request
- Deletion pipeline: logical delete -> expired object tombstone -> background garbage collection -> removed from active stores. Backup chain removal is a separate retention policy managed by retention matrix.
- Evidence & artifacts: attached are the SOC 2 summary and a retention matrix tailored to the items we discussed. We can also produce an extract of backup retention logs for a limited time period under contractual request.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll attach the retention matrix and SOC 2 summary in this thread (done).
2) Ben will kick off the vendor security questionnaire; Marcus will manage the tech follow-up to walk through any items flagged as high-risk.
3) If you want to negotiate a tighter deletion SLA (e.g., purge backups within 30 days), please indicate and we’ll surface to legal/ops for feasibility and pricing impact.

I’m available Tue/Wed 10–11am PT for a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
